title: policy-rule-consolidation-and-fallback-compat-layer
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Summary:
Refactor the policy engine's routing rule ingestion to introduce a consolidated, typed schema (JSON Schema + canonical IR) and a runtime compatibility layer that prevents silent breakages when older routing manifests are deployed. The goal is a single authoritative validator (schema + semantic checks) plus a migration toolchain that can offer autofixes and a gradual rollout path.

Motivation:
- Current DSL accepts heterogeneous configs with ad-hoc heuristics in the dispatcher. This leads to surprising fallback behavior and difficult-to-debug region/tier mismatches.
- Need deterministic validation earlier (CI / pre-commit / console upload) and predictable runtime semantics for tier routing + fallback model variants.
- Reduce on-call incidents where malformed rules cause global fallback to lower-tier models.

High-level proposal:
1) Define a strict JSON Schema and a compact typed IR (line-oriented, protobuf-friendly) that captures: selectors (region, shard), tier priorities, capacity / latency hints, and ordered fallback variants with explicit compatibility tags.
2) Implement a validator library (go/rust) with two modes: "lint" (warnings + autofix suggestions) and "enforce" (reject). Expose as: a) pre-commit hook, b) CI step, c) Console upload validator.
3) Implement a runtime compatibility shim that can accept legacy directives and translate them to the typed IR at ingestion time. The shim will emit telemetry showing which translation rules were used so we can deprecate them.
4) Provide a migration tool (cli: redwood-policy-migrate) that scans repos/configs and offers --apply autofixes for safe transformations.

Schema & semantic checks (examples):
- Region selector must include one of: {us-west, us-east, eu-west, ap-south} or a regex pattern with documented semantics.
- Tier must be one of: {realtime, burst, cost-optimized} and optionally include min_qps and max_latency_ms hints.
- Fallback list must be explicit with compatibility tags (e.g. model_v1.2+quantized). Implicit fallback to "latest" is disallowed.
- Disallow cross-region tier pins unless explicit affinity=true and capacity overrides present.

Migration plan:
- Phase 0 (this sprint): Develop JSON Schema + typed IR PoC + unit tests. Add lint mode that only warns.
- Phase 1 (next sprint): Integrate validator into CI (redwood/infra) and Console upload path. Begin telemetry for shim translations.
- Phase 2: Launch redwood-policy-migrate as beta; invite top 10 internal customers to opt-in for automated migration.
- Phase 3: After 6 weeks of metrics showing <0.5% translation events for configured fleets, flip default mode to enforce for new uploads and show remediation guidance in Console.

Rollout & observability:
- Metrics to track: translation_event_count, validator_warning_rate, validator_reject_rate, post-deploy_fallback_incidents (rate), time-to-detect-invalid-config.
- Console: add per-config validation panel that shows lint warnings, suggested fixes, and a one-click apply for managers with proper RBAC.
- Dashboards: new 'Policy Validation' dashboard under Console -> Observability; alert if validator_reject_rate > 1% for five minutes.

Acceptance criteria:
- A formal JSON Schema is checked in under docs/policy-schema/v1.json and referenced in the design doc.
- Validator library compiles and has 95% unit test coverage for schema + semantic rules.
- Migration CLI can automatically fix at least 80% of real-world legacy patterns found in a scan of historical configs (run against internal corp repo).
- Console shows validation output for upload flow and prevents risky uploads when in enforce mode.

QA & tests:
- Unit tests for schema validation and individual semantic rules.
- Integration tests: CI step rejecting intentionally malformed policies; Console upload acceptance/instrumentation tests.
- Fuzz harness: mutate existing policy corpus and assert validator doesn't crash and flags anomalies.

Security & compliance:
- The validator will run in the control plane and must not leak customer policy contents to external telemetry. Telemetry will only include hashed rule fingerprints and translation counts.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- IR format: protobuf gives performance and typing but requires migration for text-first workflows. Consider a line-oriented canonical YAML for human editing with a protobuf serialization for compactness.
- How aggressive should autofixes be? For first release we limit --apply to safe renames and explicit value normalizations.
- Do we allow runtime rewrites that change semantics (e.g., drop implicit region fallback)? We prefer conservative translation that preserves behavior until customer consents.
